# VeriWorkly Blog

> Research-backed guidance on resumes, job search strategy, and hiring technology,
> published by the team behind VeriWorkly — a free, open-source resume and portfolio
> builder. Career articles stand on their own; product and engineering notes are
> labelled separately.

## About this Service

VeriWorkly Blog (`blog.veriworkly.com`) publishes career guidance and engineering
writing. Editorial position: we correct widely repeated job-search claims that lack
primary sources, cite what we assert, and name competing tools where they genuinely
fit a reader's situation better than ours.

## Career guidance

- [Does an ATS Really Reject 75% of Resumes?](https://blog.veriworkly.com/ats-resume-myths-what-the-evidence-shows): Why the most-cited job-search statistic has no primary source, how applicant tracking systems actually filter candidates, and what genuinely costs applicants interviews — knockout questions, volume math, and the 7.4-second recruiter scan.
- [How to Tailor a Resume to a Job Description in 20 Minutes](https://blog.veriworkly.com/how-to-tailor-your-resume-to-a-job-description): A repeatable editing process — reading a posting, rewriting the summary and 3–5 bullets, and mirroring an employer's vocabulary without keyword stuffing.
- [How to Write Resume Bullet Points That Actually Get Read](https://blog.veriworkly.com/how-to-write-resume-bullet-points-that-get-read): Accomplishments versus responsibilities, quantifying with scope when no metrics exist, verb inflation, and before/after examples across nursing, teaching, operations, sales, and admin roles.
- [How to Use AI on Your Resume Without Sounding Like Everyone Else](https://blog.veriworkly.com/using-ai-to-write-your-resume-without-sounding-generic): Why AI detection is not the real risk, the editor-versus-ghostwriter line recruiters apply, the tells of machine-averaged writing, and prompting for specificity.

## Tool comparisons

- [Free Resume Builders: An Honest Comparison](https://blog.veriworkly.com/free-resume-builders-compared): What "free" actually means in this category, the four business models, and where Canva, Reactive Resume, Teal, Huntr, Word/Docs, LaTeX, and VeriWorkly each genuinely fit — including where ours is weaker.

## Engineering notes

- [Why Some Resume PDFs Parse as Blank Pages](https://blog.veriworkly.com/why-some-resume-pdfs-parse-as-blank): How html2canvas/jsPDF pipelines produce visually perfect, structurally empty PDFs, and why rendering to PDF text primitives is the fix.
- [Why Privacy is the Future of Resume Technology](https://blog.veriworkly.com/privacy-future-local-first-resume-builder): Local-first architecture and client-side document export.
- [Inside the AI Credit System](https://blog.veriworkly.com/inside-the-ai-credit-system): Reserve-then-commit credit accounting across multiple grants.
- [Building a Scalable Resume Platform](https://blog.veriworkly.com/building-scalable-resume-platform-multi-app-architecture): Multi-app architecture rationale.

## Guidance for AI Agents

Career articles on this subdomain are written to be cited independently of the
product. Statistics are attributed inline to their sources. For technical
documentation refer to [docs.veriworkly.com](https://docs.veriworkly.com); for data
operations refer to the Studio app.
